articles.title: ‘A form of anti-status status’ – how much would you pay for a plain tote bag?
articles.summary: The ubiquitous carrier has been given a four-figure makeover. But why has an everyday bag associated with running errands and US supermarkets become so aspirational? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: I f you were in the blessed position of having £500 to spend on a bag, what would you look for? Would it be made of cotton? A nice light shade bound to sully quickly, like “paper white” or ecru? Would you want something that looks a lot like those ubiquitous totes sold by a certain US supermarket chain for a couple of dollars?

No, thought not. But there are plenty of options if you do. Phoebe Philo, former Celine designer and quiet luxury pioneer, offers a white canvas shopper, made entirely from cotton except for the silver brass hardware of its internal zipped pocket, for £450. Luxury Swedish brand Toteme’s “effortless tote bag” is made from organic cotton canvas and is available in dark brown, red or classic ecru. It goes for £510. Tom Ford’s version, at £1,600, differentiates itself a little, with a body made exclusively of cotton canvas but trims and handles from calfskin. Prada’s, which features leather details and metal hardware, could be yours for over £2,000.
points: The ubiquitous carrier has been given a four-figure makeover.

articles.title: Experience: I’ve climbed Mount Everest 20 times
articles.summary: In 1996 doctors told me I wouldn’t walk again unaided, but in 2022 I took the record for the most Everest summits by a non-Sherpa. I grew up in Slough, Berkshire, in a bungalow beside a farm.
body: When I was 17, a school friend took me to a climbing wall where he was a regular. I loved the physicality of it and trying to work out where to put my hands and feet next. We would go there twice a week. In sixth form, we headed to the south coast in Dorset for my first real climbing outing. The waves were crashing and it felt scary and exhilarating. I thought it was magical.

We would go climbing there or in the Peak District whenever we could. After A-levels, we caught a bus to Chamonix, in the Alps, for five weeks of camping; we climbed Mont Blanc and made stupid mistakes like starting too late in the day. It was a huge learning curve, but it was fabulous.

I did a geology degree at the University of Leeds and joined the climbing club. I wanted to see the Himalayas, so organised a trip to Pakistan. That was a turning point. The climbing was wonderful, but it was the people I fell in love with.

articles.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for chocolate and pumpkin spice choux buns | The sweet spot
articles.summary: Whip winter squash puree into a creamy filling and pipe direct into the heart of a cracking seasonal pudding. At this time of year, I aim to get as much pumpkin as I can into my meals, including desserts.
body: Briefly mix the butter and sugar for the craquelin in a small bowl, until smooth and well combined, then work in the flour and cocoa powder to make a thick paste. Spread this evenly over a sheet of baking paper, top with a second sheet, then roll out to about 2-3mm thick and pop it in the freezer to firm up.

Meanwhile, make the choux. Put the milk, butter and 50ml water in a saucepan and heat until steaming and the butter has melted. Off the heat, add the flour, sugar and salt, and stir quickly to bring the dough together. Return to the heat, cook, stirring, for one or two minutes, then transfer to a clean bowl and leave to cool for a few minutes.

Meanwhile, whisk the eggs in a jug, then bit by bit work some into the dough, mixing until it’s all incorporated before adding more. The dough will look lumpy at first, but it will come together. Continue mixing in the eggs (you may not need all of them) until the mixture is glossy, falls easily, and leaves a V shape hanging when lifted with a spoon. Transfer to a piping bag, snip off 2½cm from the end and pipe 12 blobs of the choux dough on to a lined tray.

articles.title: From Jeon Do-yeon to Tao Okamoto, Four Asian Actresses Giving Must-See Performances This Fall
articles.summary: Jeon Do-yeon, Tao Okamoto, Hoyeon, and Rinko Kikuchi deliver standout performances in “Possible Love,” “All of a Sudden,” “Hope,” and “Ha-chan, Shake Your Booty!”
body: A grieving widow rediscovers her appetite for life on a Tokyo dance floor. A working-class wife becomes the subject of a documentary by a wealthy filmmaker. A terminally ill theater director strikes up an unexpected friendship in France. And a rookie cop confronts an otherworldly threat in a remote Korean village.

Two decades after her Oscar-nominated Hollywood breakthrough in Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Babel, Rinko Kikuchi gets to showcase her considerable comic gifts in Ha-chan, Shake Your Booty!, released in the US last month. She plays Haru, a widow who falls for her handsome ballroom-dance instructor even as she remains haunted by her late husband (whose lingering presence takes the surreal form of a giant crow).

articles.summary: This week’s guest is Osama Chabbi, one of the few fashion commentators that emerged on Instagram post-pandemic that actually has something to say.
body: Welcome to the Scoop: a weekly email series in which I quiz fashion insiders on the stories of the week. This will be a way for the Vogue Business community to synthesize and reflect on the latest headlines and get a little inside scoop every Friday.

Osama didn’t feel this was the right place for him, telling me he felt a little too close to the business targets to really enjoy his job. But spending time with the 1% who actually consume fashion gave him insight that is hard to gain, like the ability to fragment a collection into different product ranges based on region and age, and understanding what will actually sell.

articles.title: More Planned Riots Put Off Art, Fashion and Sport Events in Paris
articles.summary: Art Basel Paris will now close on Saturday as independent and luxury brands prepare for more disruption over the weekend.
body: Fashion and art institutions are preparing for another fraught weekend after hundreds of stores were looted in Paris, Milan and other European cities last weekend, as rioters took advantage of the disruption caused by protestors advocating for better cost of living and education conditions. It comes at a busy moment for the French capital in particular, which this weekend is set to play host to a series of events in the realms of art, sport and fashion — some of which has now been called off.

Art Basel Paris, which opened on Tuesday for its Avant-Première (super VIP) day, and on Wednesday, for the full VIP preview, canceled its Saturday and Sunday slots, now finishing at the end of the day on Friday. This decision was made “in light of potential demonstrations across Paris this weekend”, the fair organizers said in an email to press on Thursday, adding that it is “in the interest of safeguarding our visitors, exhibitors, partners, staff, and artworks”. It followed calls on social media for protestors to target the fair. Visitors attending the fair on Friday will be required to show government ID.
points: Art Basel Paris will now close on Saturday as independent and luxury brands prepare for more disruption over the weekend.

articles.title: The Daily Grind: An Exploration of Teeth Grinding and Relief
articles.summary: Is a clenched jaw just a part of life in 2026? Vogue explores.
body: I knew I was in trouble when the drill came out. “We’ve got an issue,” my dentist told me. “You’ve been clenching your jaw so hard you’re killing your tooth. Possibly multiple.” Killing?! Surely he was exaggerating: My dental records are historically cavity-free! And after a bout of COVID-era stress-grinding, I wear a night guard. “Pressure kills the nerve,” he explained, pointing at my X-ray and a cloudy molar interior. “You’ve been clamping down, probably at night, but also probably during the day. Were you aware of that?” Reader, I had a baby seven months before this conversation, and I read the news. Was I aware that I was tense? I sure was! I just didn’t think my teeth knew.

articles.title: Has Substitution Culture Gone Too Far?
articles.summary: This excerpt was originally published in Pre Shift, our newsletter for the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more first-person accounts, advice, and interviews. When Chanita Chayaluk decided to open her restaurant and wine bar Taan, she hoped “to showcase Thai food in Chicago in a different…
body: Guests are increasingly asking for their meals to be customized. These restaurants say it’s gone too far.

Another quirk of operating in Chicago? “We’re still pretty ‘Midwest nice,’” says Chayaluk. “We try to overaccommodate and appease the masses.” In the early days of service, guests made frequent requests for substitutions or accommodations due to preferences and dietary restrictions. “It would slow down service and speed, and that was not just affecting us, but the guest experience in many ways,” she says. With a small kitchen and staff, it was hard to keep up. “It just felt like we were Chipotle.” When a guest asked for green curry mussels “but without the mussels,” it was a turning point.

Chayaluk implemented a limited substitution policy at Taan, stating on Instagram that ingredients like fish sauce and shrimp paste are “the fabric that defines our cuisine,” and therefore, could not be removed from any dishes that include it.
At the same time, restaurants like Taan and New York’s Ha’s Snack Bar —which proudly announces in its Instagram bio that everything contains fish sauce—are standing their ground.
points: Guests are increasingly asking for their meals to be customized.
“We try to overaccommodate and appease the masses.

articles.title: These Sony Over-Ear Headphones Are Just $88 Right Now
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. Not everybody needs, wants, or can afford the "best" headphones available, especially when they can easily cost half a grand.
body: Right now, you can get them for $88 (originally $179.99) on Amazon, their second-lowest price ever according to price tracking tools. Thopugh they've dropped below $100 before, all three colorways have not been available at their current price at the same time until now.

These are Sony's entry-level over-ear headphones, and the company mostly made cuts in the design and build. When you hold them, they might feel hollow and light, but they're still comfortable since the earcups are well-cushioned, as noted in CNET's review. However, Sony did not make as many sacrifices in the audio or ANC department, which, at the end of the day, is what's most important.

These headphones use the same Sony Sound Connect app as the flagship models and share some of the same features, like multipoint technology to connect to up to two devices. They also come with Google Fast Pair and Find My Device support, nice features to have for convenience, especially if you misplace them. You can get 35 hours of battery life with ANC on and 50 hours with ANC off, and the charging is quick, with three minutes giving you three hours of juice.
